open_points.subject: A17 listener exclusivity
open_points.text: Registry opens each listener for itself alone, never with an option that lets another socket bind the same endpoint.
open_points.question: Exactly which socket options and platform behaviours are forbidden or required to ensure that no other socket can bind the endpoint?
options: Forbid only port-sharing options such as SO_REUSEPORT
Forbid every reuse option, including SO_REUSEADDR
Define the requirement behaviourally: while Registry listens, every attempted second bind to the endpoint must fail on every supported platform
open_points.default_guess: Define it behaviourally and prohibit SO_REUSEPORT; permit SO_REUSEADDR only where the supported platform still guarantees that a second live listener cannot bind the endpoint.

witness.initial: Registry has a valid complete configuration with distinct owner and service ports.
events: Registry starts and opens a listener using an option an implementer believes is harmless.
Another local process attempts to bind and listen on the same configured endpoint.
outcomes: The second bind fails, so Registry alone owns the endpoint.
The second bind succeeds because the selected reuse option permits sharing.
witness.observer: A caller whose connections may reach either listener, and the host owner inspecting the listeners.

open_points.subject: A17 formal invariants and Required tests
open_points.text: The two addresses have different ports, so that the two surfaces never share an endpoint, and Registry opens each listener for itself alone, never with an option that lets another socket bind the same endpoint.
open_points.question: Is exclusive ownership of each listening endpoint a formal invariant, and if so which Required tests item must state what is shown for both Registry surfaces and for a competing socket?
options: Add a Required tests item proving a competing bind cannot succeed while each Registry listener is open
Add a static test proving every listener is created without forbidden sharing options
Declare only the different-port configuration check an invariant and remove the untested endpoint-exclusivity guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Make endpoint exclusivity a formal invariant and require a supported-platform integration test in which a competing bind to each live endpoint fails.

witness.initial: The two configured addresses have different ports and all configuration checks pass.
events: Registry opens both listeners with a sharing option.
The existing same-port configuration test is run and passes because it tests only Registry's two configured addresses.
A second process binds one already-open Registry endpoint.
outcomes: The implementation passes every listed Required test although another listener can share Registry's endpoint.
A required competing-bind test fails and exposes the violated exclusivity invariant.
witness.observer: The release test gate and callers connecting to the shared endpoint.

open_points.subject: A21 security review after the current A17 change
open_points.text: Performed again on 2026-11-11, after that day's changes to A01, A02, A04, A07, A13, A15, A16, A17, A18 and A19 reopened it (rule 2): every category naming them — injection_interpreted_input (A02, A16, A19), secrets, authentication and concurrency (A01, A04, A07, A13, A15, A17, A18), browser_boundary (A13, A19), files_artifacts (A07, A16, A18), authorization (A04) — was reviewed;
open_points.question: Because the round states that A17 has changed since its latest review, is A21 now reopened, and which categories review the new port-range constants, different-port refusal and exclusive-listener rule before the review may again say PERFORMED?
options: A21 is reopened and the affected categories must be reviewed and recorded
The current A17 changes were already included in the quoted 2026-11-11 review, which must be stated explicitly with their outcomes
The changes affect no security-review category, which must be recorded as the result of reopening the review
open_points.default_guess: Treat A21 as reopened, review at least authentication_credential_abuse, browser_boundary, dependencies and any network-boundary implications, then record the resulting unchanged or changed outcomes.

witness.initial: A21's latest recorded performance considered the earlier A17 changes, while the current round says A17 changed after that review.
events: The new port-separation and listener-exclusivity rules are accepted.
A release proceeds either treating the existing PERFORMED line as current or treating rule 2 as reopening the review.
outcomes: The security review remains marked PERFORMED without examining the new listener behaviour.
The review is pending until the affected categories examine and record the new listener behaviour.
witness.observer: The security reviewer and any release gate relying on A21's status.
